questions.stem: Two events are mutually exclusive if:

options.text: They cannot happen at the same time

questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur at the same time. If one happens, the other cannot.

questions.stem: For mutually exclusive events $A$ and $B$, $P(A \text{ or } B) =$
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events, the addition rule simplifies to $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B)$ because $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0$.

questions.stem: A fair dice is rolled. What is $P(\text{rolling a 2 or a 5})$?
questions.explanation: Rolling a 2 and rolling a 5 are mutually exclusive. $P(2 \text{ or } 5) = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.stem: Which pair of events is NOT mutually exclusive?

options.text: Drawing a red card and drawing a king from a deck
Drawing a heart and drawing a spade from a deck
Rolling an even number and rolling an odd number on a dice
Getting heads and getting tails on a single coin flip

questions.explanation: A card can be both red and a king (e.g. king of hearts or king of diamonds), so these events are not mutually exclusive.

questions.stem: If $P(A) = 0.4$, $P(B) = 0.3$, and $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, what is $P(A \text{ or } B)$?
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive events: $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7$.

questions.stem: If all possible outcomes are mutually exclusive and cover every possibility, their probabilities must:
questions.explanation: If the outcomes are exhaustive (cover every possibility) and mutually exclusive, their probabilities must sum to 1.

questions.stem: A bag has 5 red, 3 blue, and 2 yellow balls. What is the probability of picking a red or yellow ball?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow are mutually exclusive: $P(\text{red or yellow}) = \frac{5}{10} + \frac{2}{10} = \frac{7}{10}$.
